headline: Chief Prelates’ letter on judicial retirement age made public
caption: The MP displays the letter at a media briefing in Colombo.
body: Colombo, Aug. 12 (Island Chronicle) - An opposition parliamentarian on Wednesday (12) made public a letter sent by the Chief Prelates of the country's three principal Buddhist Chapters to the President, urging the Government not to proceed with a proposed constitutional amendment to extend the retirement age of superior court judges.
Speaking at a media briefing, the MP said he had obtained a copy of the letter and decided to make its contents public amid recent political discussion surrounding the proposed amendment.
According to the letter, the Chief Prelates pointed out that the Constitution currently sets the retirement age at 63 for Court of Appeal judges and 65 for Supreme Court judges.
“We believe that it is not appropriate for the Government to act in this manner to increase those age limits,” the letter states, according to the section released at the briefing.
The Chief Prelates urged the Government to reconsider the proposed amendment, expressing concerns over any move to extend the retirement age of superior court judges.

headline: Port throughput climbs 11% as transhipment volumes recover
caption: Container operations at the main terminal earlier this month.
body: Colombo, Aug. 12 (Island Chronicle) - Container throughput at the country's main port rose 11 percent year-on-year in July, driven largely by a recovery in transhipment volumes, according to figures released by the ports authority this week.
Officials attributed the increase to the return of several regional feeder services and improved berth productivity following the commissioning of additional gantry cranes.
Industry representatives cautioned that sustaining the growth would depend on continued investment in landside infrastructure, noting that yard congestion remained a constraint during peak weeks.
The authority said a detailed quarterly review would be published later this month.

headline: Reservoir levels stabilise after late monsoon rainfall
caption: Water levels at a central highlands reservoir this week.
body: Kandy, Aug. 12 (Island Chronicle) - Reservoir levels across the central highlands have stabilised following late monsoon rainfall, easing concerns over irrigation supply for the coming cultivation season, officials said on Wednesday.
The irrigation department reported that major reservoirs were collectively at 68 percent of capacity, up from 54 percent a month earlier.
Farmers' organisations welcomed the improvement but called for clearer guidance on release schedules ahead of planting.
A departmental spokesperson said allocation decisions would be announced after consultations with district-level committees.
